_source: Shipped example record set for the ranked-choice tabulation project templates/obligations.example.json declares: one single-execution invariant record (A1) and one multi-execution system-claim record (S1) whose cohort covers every tool ID in S1's required_evidence. Field order, field set, and the derivation of the record-level legacy bindings from executions[0] are exactly what tools/evidence-run.ts writes; the envelope around `records` is the one-file form Gate B's load_records unwraps (a producer writes one bare record per file at .fv/evidence/records/<claim_id>.json). Record semantics: docs/dogfood-evidence.md.

_materialization.convention: Every <angle-bracketed> value is a PLACEHOLDER and no shipped file can carry its real value: these digests bind to one project tree and to the executables of one machine. Materialize them before the set means anything - a record carrying a placeholder digest is rejected by Gate B, not tolerated by it.
placeholder_fields: bindings.source_snapshot - `scripts/fv_project.py snapshot`; one value shared by every record of one run
bindings.intent_hash - SHA-256 over the resolved canonical target's bytes (.fv/intent.md here, since this project declares no omp_native.target_spec)
bindings.toolchain_digests.executable and .sha256, and the same two fields of every executions[] entry - absolute path of the resolved launched executable and SHA-256 over its bytes
bindings.raw_output_hash and every executions[].raw_output_hash - SHA-256 over that execution's raw log bytes
_materialization.literal_fields: claim_id, required, evidence_class, result, scope, profile, required_targets, environment_policy, command, configuration, seeds, run_id, raw_output_path, and every executions[] field not listed above are literal. raw_output_path is derivable rather than captured: under profile producer-trusted-execution it is exactly .fv/evidence/raw/<claim_id>-<execution run_id>.log. toolchain_digests.version and .version_exit_code are illustrative captured text - Gate B checks their types, not their content.

# Intent: ranked-choice tabulation

A1: no candidate is eliminated while tied for the minimum tally.
S1: the protocol model, the proved tally core, and the contract entry point agree on eliminated-candidate ordering.

_materialization.project_layout_note: .fv/obligations.json is templates/obligations.example.json copied verbatim: its bytes are what bindings.obligation_manifest_hash binds, so a reformatting edit stales this whole set. The paths above are the tree the commands and cwds below presume; a git repository over them is what makes the verified-input snapshot computable.

.fv/evidence/raw/A1-2026-09-15T11-42-07-: Complete - 1 successfully verified harnesses, 0 failures, 1 total.
.fv/evidence/raw/S1-2026-09-15T11-58-02-: Complete - 1 successfully verified harnesses, 0 failures, 1 total.

_materialization.raw_artifact_note: Each list above is one raw log's captured output without its trailer. The producer appends exactly one canonical trailer line as the log's last line, and Gate B rejects a PASS artifact that carries two of them or ends anywhere else, so materialize each log as the lines above followed by raw_artifact_trailer, each line newline-terminated.
_materialization.gate_note: No --expect-snapshot, no --expect-intent, no --allow-unbound: the gate recomputes the verified-input snapshot and the intent hash itself and answers VERDICT: VERIFIED[profile=producer-trusted-execution] with binding=recomputed. tests/r37_evidence_examples.py performs this materialization in a temporary git project and asserts that verdict, so the example is machine-validated rather than illustrated.
